title: Mexico Became the World’s Largest Beer Exporter in 2025
author: the La Jornada editorial staff
content:
_This article by the La Jornada editorial staff originally appeared in
the[August 7, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/08/07/economia/cerveza-
mexicana-logro-en-2025-exportaciones-por-6-mil-480-mdd-sader), Mexico’s
premier left-wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. In 2025, Mexican beer reached consumers in 98 countries and
its exports totaled sales of US$6.48 billion, the Secretariat of Agriculture
and Rural Development (Sader) reported. The agency specified that **Mexico
maintained an average share of 36 percent of the value of global beer
exports** during that period, rising from US$5.618 billion in 2021 to US$6.48
billion in 2025, as a result of its growing competitiveness, quality, and
international recognition.

With this result, it took first place among the leading beer-exporting
countries, thereby far surpassing the Netherlands, Belgium, and Germany.

Among the five main destinations for the Mexican beverage are the United
States, with US$6.046 billion; the Dominican Republic, with US$49 million;
Spain, with US$39 million; Peru, with US$37 million; and Panama, with US$32
million, as of the close of 2025.

To these are added the Netherlands, with US$31 million; Guatemala, with US$27
million; Puerto Rico, with US$20 million; Honduras, with US$14 million; El
Salvador, with US$13 million; and other nations, with US$173 million.

On International Beer Day, celebrated each first Friday of August, it noted
that Mexico sustained an average annual volume of 4.316 billion liters over
the last five years—that is, it went from shipping 4.253 billion liters to
4.285 billion liters.

These results reflect the productive capacity—particularly of Mexican
producers of malted cereals such as barley, wheat, and corn—the quality and
safety of Mexican agro-industry, and the joint work with federal and state
authorities to strengthen competitiveness and expand the presence of Mexican
products in international markets.

The Secretariat of Agriculture and Rural Development, headed by Columba Jazmín
López Gutiérrez, reaffirmed its commitment to promoting programs and projects
that strengthen the productivity, innovation, and competitiveness of the beer
production chain, in order to generate greater opportunities for producers,
promote the country’s economic development, and maintain Mexico’s leadership
in the international trade of agro-industrial foods and beverages.
